issues.title: More private utilities that need to be marked and public api deprecated
issues.body:
In types.py
- [ ]  `convert_type` - rename to _convert_type - currently has no top level import
- [ ] `FuncParamType` - maybe typing thing? - currently has no top level import

In _ ?,
- [ ] consider deprecating 'open_file'
issues.author: Rowlando13

comments.body:
Should `open_file` and `safecall` be made private as well?

I'm looking at adapting `pip-tools` to handle v8.5.0 this morning, and we have (this all looks weird to me)...
```python
my_file = click.open_file(filename, "w+b", atomic=True, lazy=True)
assert my_file is not None
if isinstance(my_file, click.utils.LazyFile):
    ctx.call_on_close(click.utils.safecall(my_file.close_intelligently))
```

I don't see any reason that anyone outside of `click` should ever use `safecall`: it's trivial to write it yourself. `open_file` doesn't seem good to expose if its return type won't be exposed. It's hard to figure out how to use it correctly in this case.

(We do want `close_intelligently()` since the target filename could be `"-"`.)
comments.author: sirosen

comments.body: safe call is deprecated. It should issue a deprecation warning. I will have to check on the other.
comments.author: Rowlando13

comments.body: We will have to look at open_file. It is public on purpose but may need better type annotation or docs.
comments.author: Rowlando13

comments.body:
I didn't want to suggest too much at first, but maybe we can spec it out with a `typing.Protocol`? I'm happy to help out if you want to go that route.

And yeah, I didn't notice that `safecall` was also warning, since I fixed this "all at once" on my end.
comments.author: sirosen

comments.body: Feel free to open an issue and propose a PR for what you think is best. I am always interested in type hints or docs that make usage clearer.
comments.author: Rowlando13

comments.body: I feel like `open_file` should be private, but I haven't looked enough. `atomic` should be deprecated, if I remember correctly it's not actually atomic and there are better libraries out there for atomic access. `lazy` is only useful for the `File` param type when opening a file for writing, and should be invisible to the public API. It shouldn't matter if it's lazy, it should just close silently.
comments.author: davidism

comments.body:
Aside: I didn't suggest a protocol because I didn't come up with a good name or home for it. Which might be a sign that it's not a great idea.

I'm not aware of a good, supported library for atomic/transactional writes. So if it becomes private, I'll probably review [this old thread](https://discuss.python.org/t/adding-atomicwrite-in-stdlib/11899) (which has lots of good notes and ideas) and roll my own. Which I'm okay with.

From my perspective:
- it's weird that `open_file` is exposed at all; it feels orthogonal to most of the concerns of `click` (even though it will be a pain for me, I'm in favor of making it private)
- it's arguable that even implementing `lazy=True` is outside of what `click` should be doing

I'm using `LazyFile` in a few places today, but I feel like the ideal path is to put together something that's a replacement and can be passed as a param type, but outside of `click`. Let the core library stay lean and focused.
comments.author: sirosen

comments.body:
> it feels orthogonal to most of the concerns of click

Yes, this is a general problem with the pallets libraries exposing so many utilities and customization points. We're trying to clean this up in general. See for example the next Werkzeug 3.2 release, which is a huge wall of deprecations.
comments.author: davidism

comments.body:
The library I was thinking of was [atomicwrites](https://github.com/untitaker/python-atomicwrites), which is archived in favor of [`os.replace`](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/os.html#os.replace) or [`os.rename`](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/os.html#os.rename). Those are both documented as atomic.

The simplest answer for lazy is probably to use `Path` instead of `File` param types, and handle opening the file yourself when you write. That's probably a lot simpler than all the stuff we have to go through for `File` anyway.
comments.author: davidism

> Are there any known issues with 3.14? I've been using 8.3.1 with 3.14 and it seems to be well-supported.

No issues yet, but also there is no declaration of support. I was checking when 3.14 was added to CI and found that the related commit hasn't been included in a release yet.

> Click has always supported 3.14.

I'm not sure what "always" means in this context but I guess you mean it didn't cause any issues yet.

I was planning to use click for another library I'm preparing to release. It will declare support for 3.14, and I was trying to select a min version for click too, by looking for the earliest version that is tested with 3.14. That release doesn't exist yet, and it turns out click doesn't declare support for any Python version at all (no Python minors in the trove classifiers), which I find rather unfortunate from a maintainer's perspective.

If the 8-year-old decision to not manage trove classifiers can be revisited, I'm willing to create a PR to add them.

---

Thanks for the quick response and merry Christmas / happy New Year! 🎄

<details>

```

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\Users\Emory\AppData\Local\Python\pythoncore-3.14-64\Lib\site-packages\click\_termui_impl.py", line 729, in edit_files
    c = subprocess.Popen(
        args=shlex.split(editor) + list(filenames),
        env=environ,
    )
  File "C:\Users\Emory\AppData\Local\Python\pythoncore-3.14-64\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1038, in __init__
    self._execute_child(args, executable, preexec_fn, close_fds,
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
                        pass_fds, cwd, env,
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    ...<5 lines>...
                        gid, gids, uid, umask,
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
                        start_new_session, process_group)
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "C:\Users\Emory\AppData\Local\Python\pythoncore-3.14-64\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1552, in _execute_child
    hp, ht, pid, tid = _winapi.CreateProcess(executable, args,
                       ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
                             # no special security
                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    ...<4 lines>...

    raise ClickException(
        _("{editor}: Editing failed: {e}").format(editor=editor, e=e)
```

```py
import click
```

- Click version: 8.5.0
- OS: Windows 11 (64-bit)

comments.body:
I tried recreating the issue on my own system: `windows 11 build number (26100.9445)`, `python version 3.14`, and also checked for Notepad execution alias toggle which was default nothing to change, but I couldn't recreate it , tested it for for total 30 iterations no failures not even one.
Then I investigated the issue from different paths, and perspectives : first - I tired to crosscheck shlex working and how it is used in the codebase, as `shlex` is based on unix systems, so it treats backslashes differently which can cause an error but as 'notepad' passed directly Nothing could be wrong here( it’s single string so no split), and environment which was passed in click function, was just copy of original one Nothing changed.So that completely eliminated any parsing issue, or conditional check issue as error messages suggested.
So next thing i dig up was, windows error which were mentioned : `INVALID_PARAMETER` and `ERROR_SXS_CANT_GEN_ACTCTX`, I explored few articles on this , one was completely related to this ( it is from Microsoft's own Q&A platform) , and it’s main point was that crash inside a specific alias-resolution dll, is inconsistent or random getting 4 times out of 10 time failures( same condition as described in the this issue description ), but it pointed to alias thing which again i tried to debug and analyse it ( as many users have experience this issue, regarding notepad specifically in windows).
And as i couldn't recreate the error, it is currently too vague to work on a solution and from my conclusion it seems like a know windows platform bug rather than click functionality error, here's is a thread to support this (<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/2109069/createprocess-on-notepad-exe-fails-due-to-a-crash>) , and as in the thread, someone already tested with full exe path too, but it did not succeed as per them.
I would like to know the maintainers view on this particular issue, and about my findings.
